name: Chondrostereum purpureum

t_opt.note: from the abstract: cultures from yellow birch grew at 5 to 35 C, fastest at 25 C. The family minimum (4 C) and maximum (38 C) are left in place; they agree with growth at 5 C and with most New Zealand isolates still growing at 36 C (Spiers et al. 2000, Mycological Research 104:395-402, abstract)
t_opt.source: Wall RE 1986, Pathogenicity of Chondrostereum purpureum to yellow birch, Plant Disease 70:158-160

ecology.substrate: fresh wounds and stumps of broadleaf trees

notes: Enters fresh wounds (the survey codes it MAT/HOST); its toxin silvers leaves far from the mycelium. Reported (unchecked) to be sold as a stump-killing treatment.
